# `lead` commands

## `lead archive`

Archive or restore a lead in ordinary lists, retaining lifecycle, notes and open follow-ups.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | crm.write |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/lead.archive` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow lead archive 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 3 --reason "File enquiry" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "lead archive", "input": {"lead": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 3}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lead` | `LEAD` | string | yes | no | — | Stable lead ID or an exact unambiguous display name. Duplicate names require an ID.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | Version returned by lead show.; minimum 1 |
| `archived` | `--archived` | boolean | no | no | true | — |

## `lead close`

Close a lead with the command reason and an optional duplicate link; open follow-ups remain open.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `lead convert`

Confirm-first: convert a lead to a new top-level customer (native customer validation; name, address, contacts and summary copied, nothing financial invented) or link it to an existing customer (link only unless contact_transfers names exact fields). Run --dry-run to preview copied fields, contact mapping and matching customers. One reversible batch; `batch reverse` undoes it while nothing later depends on the customer. Example: {"lead": "01J...", "expected_version": 2, "target": "new"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | crm.convert |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/lead.convert` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow lead convert 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 2 --target new --dry-run --reason "Won the work" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "lead convert", "input": {"lead": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 2, "target": "new"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lead` | `LEAD` | string | yes | no | — | Stable lead ID or an exact unambiguous display name. Duplicate names require an ID.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | Version returned by lead show.; minimum 1 |
| `target` | `--target` | literal["new", "existing"] | yes | no | — | new: create a top-level customer from the lead through native customer validation; existing: link the lead to an existing customer, copying nothing unless contact_transfers names it. |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Existing customer ID or exact unambiguous name; required for target existing. |
| `customer_expected_version` | `--customer-expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Version returned by customer show; required for target existing. |
| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer name for target new; defaults to the lead display name. Customer names are unique. |
| `contact_transfers[].lead_contact` | inside `--contact-transfers` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Lead contact ID to copy from.; minimum length 26; maximum length 26 |
| `contact_transfers[].customer_contact` | inside `--contact-transfers` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Existing customer contact ID to copy the named fields onto; null adds the lead contact as a new additional customer contact. |
| `contact_transfers[].fields` | inside `--contact-transfers` JSON array | array[string] | no | no | [] | Contact fields to copy onto an existing customer contact (display_name, names, phones, emails, website). Nothing is overwritten that is not named here. Ignored when customer_contact is null. |

## `lead import`

Import prospects keyed by a source and a per-row source key: a repeated row is unchanged, a row whose key returns with different values refuses, and new rows land one by one in one reversible batch per source, so a failed run resumes by running it again. Also needs import and crm.write. `batch reverse` closes and archives unused imported leads and releases their keys. Example: {"source": "fair-2026", "rows": [{"source_key": "17", "display_name": "Ada Lane"}]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | crm.bulk |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/lead.import` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow lead import --source fair-2026 --rows '[{"source_key":"17","display_name":"Ada Lane"}]' --reason "Trade fair list" --json`

### MCP


## `lead reopen`

Reopen a closed lead explicitly; its notes and follow-ups retain their identities.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |

## `lead update`

Edit lead identity and stable contact collections with an expected version.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | crm.write |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/lead.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow lead update 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 1 --rating warm --reason "Qualified enquiry" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "lead update", "input": {"lead": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 1, "rating": "warm"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/lead.update`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
